Sifiso Mkhwanazi

By: Sinethemba Nogude | Commission

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
Joburg prowler Sifiso Mkhwanazi

In the heart of downtown Joburg, a series of gruesome murders sends shockwaves through the community. The perpetrator, known as Sifiso Mkhwanazi, emerges as a shadowy figure, leaving behind a trail of death and devastation. As law enforcement agencies scramble to apprehend the elusive killer, a chilling portrait begins to emerge of a man driven by dark impulses and a twisted sense of purpose…Found guilty of killing 6 sex workers , and the possibility of many more victims, we look into what drove one of the country’s youngest serial killers and the investigation that led to his arrest.

Script:


Sifiso Mkhwanazi :

Upsound Activist 04:21 That a lot of people go missing and nothing is done about it because people,like it's difficult to check people who you meet On the streets. Is that what you think is maybe one of the challenges when it comes to this case, Kazfiso, that women were missing or women were being killed ,go missing and nobody is actually tracking where these women are other than their loved ones?

Upsound detective Mbonambi : 41:23 And then obviously the father will tell him, oh, you close up when you're done. Then you will close, but very late. So I will think intentionally so, just to make sure that it's late, then you can go to the street. And then he will used one of the bakkies, his father's Bakkie i that was parked in the factory. And then he will just go to the street randomly, so he will pick up a person. // 44:42 And that section was not used also. It was upstairs. So this is where now He'll take the woman kill them in that room upstairs. And there afterwards, we now know from the investigation of the forensic in the stairs that the stairways that going up to that room, there was blood also. So it tells you after killing them, you'll then drag them down.
Upsound witness (hidden identity)06:39That was when that lady had disappeared, right? Yeah. So maybe you can talk me through that day. What happened? What is the first thing that happened? And then what happened after that? Because that guy used to come every Sunday. So he come and then he goes round and round. And then after maybe some hours of checking, he takes the lady. And then that lady was standing. And then I just saw him enter with a, like, it was a blue bag. I'm not sure.
Upsound Sergeant Mbonambi :19:44 It won't make sense that you rape a person. Okay, according to him, the sex was consensual. Then you have a consensual sex with a person. Thereafter, you kill the person. How? We know now that he agrees that he strangled them, except the one that he shot in the head.
Music swells, flashing between shots of Mkhwanazi's
Close-up of a judge delivering judgemment Clip 00021 court visuals : 16:43 On account 3, I find the accused guilty of murder read together with the provisions of section 51, subsection 1 of Act 105 of 1997. 16:25I find the accused guilty of rape read with the provisions of section 51, subsection 2 of act 105 of 1997.//
Upsound Captain Saunders 27:35So do you believe that had he not been caught he would continue? Yes, as the psychiatrist and the psychologist came and testified, they asked him the same question. And he said, I will continue killing. He said that with his own... He said to the psychiatrist and the psychologist, and they testified it in court, if he was not caught, he would have continued and would kill more. It was not done
[fade to black into drone visuals of Joburg ]

Link : Downtown Johannesburg, life here is especially harsh for women. Desperation pushes many into sex work, where danger is ever-present. Vulnerable to violence and exploitation, they survive each night on the edge, with no safety—only the constant fear of what may come.
[breather]
V/O Something especially true when there’s a serial killer on the loose.

[transition/breather]

Upsound Noxolo Khumalo 23:05 My mother was a very lovely person. outgoing, outspoken. She loved dancing. [ Claire]She loved life. Very much. She loved life.

V/O: In September 2022, Noxolo Khumalo’s mother, Chihota Nyarai, went missing while working on the streets.

Upsound Claire Noxolo Interview 16:23 Soyou knew that your mother was a sex worker?

Upsound Noxolo Khumalo 16:34Obviously, that's not something that I can be proud of, but At the end of the day, she's still my mother. I'm gonna love her with whatever she's doing.

[breather]

Upsound Noxolo Khumalo 23:05 She was not just my mother, she was my friend // 01:07 Me and my mum would call each other every one hour, two hours, just to check up on each other.

V/O When she didn't call as usual, it set off immediate alarm bells

Upsound Noxolo Khumalo 01:07Okay, so me and my mum would call each other every one hour, two hours, just to check up on each other. So, something we're used to, it's our daily routine. If I don't call her, she calls me. If she doesn't call me, I call her. So, it was on a Sunday. I called her around three, we spoke. I called her around six, we spoke. Then I was supposed to call again around eight. Her phone went voicemail.// 01:56 I tried calling again, said maybe she went somewhere. She didn't answer, called her sisters, they went to check for her. She was not there.


Upsound Noxolo Khumalo 30:06 We were going to the mortuaries, to the police stations, hospitals, calling people, her friends, telling her if you see her, if you hear anything from her, please tell us. Walk down the streets. And we posted on social media,We went to report her missing.

[breather/ maybe some sort of timelapse]

News reports ENCA:00:00 Now the discovery of six bodies in a panel beating shop in the Joburg CBD, when the police were called to investigate a foul smell.
News report Newsroom Afrika: 00:09 The bodies are believed to be those of sex workers.
[breather]
V/O IN OCTOBER 2022, a month after Chihota Nyarai disappeared, the bodies of six female sex workers were discovered at THIS panel beater's in downtown Johannesburg. A gruesome find that dominated national headlines...Captain Vincent Saunders led the investigation.

Upsound Captain Saunders: 00:53 Our biology unit was there. Dog unit was there to take photos, to take DNA.
V/O CAPT SAUNDERS called in top detective, Sergeant Prince Mbonambi, to examine the crime scenes
Upsound Mbonambi Ooof! There was that smell that stayed with me for months.
[breather]

V/O Noxolo’s worst fears were confirmed—her mother was amongst the victims found.

Upsound Noxolo Khumalo 07:37 [Claire]At that point, had you accepted that that was Umama there and she had passed away? Or are you thinking, here's Umama, Uzovela somewhere, she's going to appear because that was not her. I didn't accept that she was the one. Just hoping that, okay, one day she's just going to show up.

[ transition ]

V/OThe prime suspect was the son of the panelbeaters’ owner, 19-year-old Sifiso Mkhwanazi.

Upsound Claire :Tell me your impression of the accused.

Upsound Captain Saunders: 12:43 he was not the person of speaking a lot of words. Very calm, very quiet.he comes as a person very cold.



V/O Under the cover of darkness, Mkhwanazi stalked the streets, on the hunt for vulnerable sex workers.

Upsound Sergeant Mkhwanazi on the weekends, He will just wait for everyone to go. make sure that it's late, he will use one of the bakkies, his father's Bakkie. And then he will just go to the street randomly, so he will pick up a person.

[breather]

Upsound Zimbabwean Witness: 06:39 that guy used to come every Sunday. So he come and then he round and round. And then after maybe some hours of checking, he take the lady. AAnd then I just saw him enter with a,. I'm not sure. 07:09 about color but the car, it was a twin cab

V/O This woman witnessed the abduction of one of the victims…

Upsound Zimbabwean Wtiness 07:31That lady never goes for one night. And then after like some days, three days, I said, it's better to go and report
Upsound Zimbabwean Wtiness08:40 Does this make you worry about your safety? You say that you weren't really that scared to go with people in their cars. But does it make you worry now about your safety? We want you to be safe out there. Like now I'm very, very scared to go with a person with a car. The person I don't know especially. Makes me scared. We are not safe.

V/O This CCTV footage shows one of Mkhwanazi’s final victims arriving at the panel beater's shop with him … she gets out of the vehicle and they walk in together.

V/O For over six months in 2022, Mkhwanazi lured women to this building. The sheer size of the location meant their bodies remained hidden until October that year when the caretaker stumbled upon human remains, leading to the gruesome discovery by police.

Upsound Mbonambi here was this body that was inside a chimney , a steel chimney.//03:07
decomposed to the last degree, the next one, it was inside the bin. Also decomposed. Ione was at the back of the panel van a body that was put in the oil, lighted up, and then And then in the truck, there was a body in the bin also. And then.... Complete skeleton.
I'll a that was the first body that he might have killed. And there was a complete skeleton body…

4.V/O The skeletal remains were believed to be those of Mkhwanazi’s first victim.

[PAUSE]

V/O A room on the third floor of this building… is now known as the slaughterhouse room…

Upsound Sergeant Mbonambi :He broke the door handle. So even if you’re passing by and you want to open, you can’t because there’s no door handle. Only him, he knows how to open.I think we used, might have used a spade to open it or something.

V/O He kept the women bound, gagged, and repeatedly raped them before eventually strangling them… two of the victims were pregnant.


Upsound Sergeant Mbonambi There was blood on the floor. A lot of fluid as well. And then there was some underwears.48:18There was human hair.48:21there was a lot of condoms. 4The used ones and unused

V/O Investigators were able to connect Mkhwanazi to the murders through DNA evidence collected from the crime scenes.

Upsound Sergeant Mbonambi 44:42 And that section was not used also. It was upstairs. So This is where now we'll take the woman and kill them in that room upstairs. And there afterwards,in the stairs that the stairways that going up to that room, there was blood also.45:12 drag them down to the floor where now He'll dispose of the bodies,

V/O What puzzled detectives was that Chihota Nyarai had been shot in the head, a departure from Mkhwanazi's usual method.

Upsound Captain Saunders 33:20 So I don't know why he was fighting with her. Maybe she was tough to die. And all that one things around in there she didn't have. She was the hand was only tight in front.

Upsound Claire question Mbonambi interview 54:28So what is the theory behind the one woman who was shot? Because you said that the others weren't shot. What happened there? What was the difference with her?

Upsound Sergeant Mbonambi 54:44Even though we were hoping to get more details on his admission, but he evaded all of those details.// 55:47was he shot. I don't know why, but my thinking is that She might have put up a fight with him and then upon realizing he was losing the fight, then he decided to shoot the woman.

[ /breather]

Upsound Noxolo khumalo 14:03 Do you still have unanswered questions? that you are still wanting answers to and what are they? Yes, I do have a lot of unanswered questions[ breather ]Why did he do it?
[Transition]

Upsound Gerard Labuschagne: Again, the scenes themselves probably wouldn't be that different to a lot of scenes that an experienced investigator would have already been on to in their career. Sure. Just backtracking a bit. So was there some kind of release or relief that Nkwanazi says he got every time he murdered the person? So Mkhwanazi didn't specify exactly how he felt after each murder, but you would normally find that there's 06:24in a way that it's a build up to what's something you want to do. Now, whether it was positive or negative for you, it's over and it's done. So we usually do find that there is a sense of relief or relief that it's over or relief that you've done it

V/O Forensic psychologist Dr. Gerard Labuschagne interviewed Mkhwanazi ahead of his trial.

Upsound Gerard:01:54 He said to me after my release from custody for the false allegation in his view. If the sex worker, we did the transaction, there was no fighting, no arguments, no arguing about more money, then she would go home safely. And there are statements of a woman who had been picked up by him during, in between these murders and released, and he didn't do anything to them. But he said, if the sex worker started to argue about money.. 02:20started to threaten that she's gonna call the cops and open up a case if he doesn't pay more, then he knew he was going to end up killing her.

While Mkhwanazi’s motives remain unclear, some believe there ARE clues in his past. At 18, he was arrested for raping a sex worker and spent 10 months in prison, a crime he denied committing.



[breather]
Upsound Captain Saunders 22:53So I think it was, I think, unjust to him. It's not that he's a criminal, you know, I don't call him a victim, and then murdered by that one, I think they was wrong. I think they, I think something happened to him in prison. I told him, I'm damn sure, I think something happened to him in prison. If that was not Pollsmorr to say that, and he's so young, they would have raped him there.//22:05 But when he came out, he came about getting his justice in this dark way

[transition visuals ]
Upsound Judgement by Judge Moosa: 15:06 In the circumstances, I reject the version of the accused, as set out in the Section 220 admissions as beyond false, and find that the accused had acted with premeditation planning and had formed an intention to kill the deceased. Further, having due regard to the totality of the evidence before this Court, 15:31and the necessary inferences that may be drawn there from, I find that the accused did unlawfully have sexual intercourse with all the deceased. I further find that the accused did unlawfully and intentionally defeat and obstruct the course of justice by concealing the bodies of the deceased.

V/O Mkhwanazi was convicted on six counts of rape, murder, and defeating the ends of justice. He was sentenced to six life terms, plus an additional 170 years behind bars.

Upsound Claire Sergeant Mbonambi: 26:57 Were you happy with the sentencing?


Upsound Sergeant Mbonambi30:24 As far as a police officer. I'm happy because we had sleepless nights with the captain working on this case. So obviously, we wanted conviction, and we've got conviction. So yes, as a police officer, I'm happy. For the families, I'm happy.


Upsound Captain Saunders: 30:33 Is it just on to the next? Yes, you feel satisfied, justice has been done, but I always say is you will never bring that people back. They won't, even if you get 20 lives, you will never bring that mother, the daughter, the sister, the aunt back. They are gone forever.



V/O While justice has been served, three of the victims remain unidentified, their families still in the dark, But for those who have found closure,They refuse to let this tragedy define them.

Upsound Noxolo Khumalo 32:10Nothing in this last cut case. They say it is asking for apology He's apologizing to the family, but he doesn't look like someone who's sorry for what he did at all You don't accept that apology. I Personally have accepted his apology. I'm not one to hold grudges He's gonna have to take it up with God and not me I've let him go off my heart and I've forgiven him not gonna hold anything against him …He has to take it up with God.

[ end]

metadata.Unique Selling Point: Joburg prowler Sifiso Mkhwanazi In the heart of downtown Joburg, a series of gruesome murders sends shockwaves through the community. The perpetrator, known as Sifiso Mkhwanazi, emerges as a shadowy figure, leaving behind a trail of death and devastation. As law enforcement agencies scramble to apprehend the elusive killer, a chilling portrait begins to emerge of a man driven by dark impulses and a twisted sense of purpose…Found guilty of killing 6 sex workers , and the possibility of many more victims, we look into what drove one of the country’s youngest serial killers and the investigation that led to his arrest.
